item.title: NASA clears its Artemis moon rocket for an April launch with four astronauts following repairs
item.description: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — NASA cleared its moon rocket on Thursday for an April launch with four astronauts after completing the latest round of repairs. item.title: Louisiana senator seeks help from EPA as invasive pest threatens rice crops
item.description: Sen. John Kennedy (R-La.) wrote a letter to the EPA Administrator requesting approval for the use of the pesticide buprofezin to fight rice delphacid infestations in Louisiana.

item.title: Crash on Florida Boulevard leaves 3 people injured
item.description: BATON ROUGE, La. (Louisiana First) — Three people were taken to a hospital following a crash in Baton Rouge on Thursday afternoon. It happened in the 9800 block of Florida Boulevard around 4:15 p.m. EMS confirmed the patients were taken to the hospital in stable condition. It is unclear what led up to the crash. [...]

item.title: Gen. Russel Honoré urges hurricane readiness in West Baton Rouge
item.description: Retired Gen. Russel Honoré addressed more than 250 people in West Baton Rouge regarding hurricane preparedness. The presentation focused on the importance of early preparation and safety measures for older residents.

item.title: NWS confirms 6 tornadoes across southeast Louisiana after Wednesday night storms
item.description: The National Weather Service office in New Orleans has confirmed six tornadoes across southeast Louisiana following severe storms that moved through the region Wednesday night.

item.title: Louisiana retired Lieutenant General urges US to pursue cease-fire with Iran
item.description: Retired Lt. Gen. Russel Honoré is calling for the United States government to pursue a cease-fire with Iran and withdraw military forces from the region.

item.title: Southern University Men's Basketball reaches SWAC semifinals after beating Arkansas-Pine Bluff
item.description: The Southern University Men's Basketball team advances to the SWAC Semifinals after an 84-81 win over the University of Arkansas-Pine Bluff.

item.title: Danish expert calls for talks with Gov. Landry on Greenland
item.description: Frederik Waage, a Danish constitutional law professor, is visiting Baton Rouge this week to speak with scholars at Louisiana State University about the ongoing controversy surrounding Greenland. Waage intends to spend several days in the city and hopes to meet with Gov. Jeff Landry to discuss the territory's status.

item.title: Residents raise concerns over potential Port Allen warehouse detention facility
item.description: Residents in West Baton Rouge Parish are speaking out after leaked federal documents suggested a warehouse in Port Allen could potentially be converted into a detention facility housing hundreds of people.
